sections.h2: Where is the city of Florence, SC, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Florence is a city of 39,899 people in the coastal plain of northeastern South Carolina, and it is the seat of Florence County. It was the tenth most populous city in the state at the 2020 census and covers 23.49 square miles, about 1,705 people per square mile.

It sits where Interstate 20 ends and Interstate 95 passes through. US 52, US 76 and US 301 also serve it. I-20 runs about 83 miles west to Columbia and I-95 runs about 87 miles northeast to Fayetteville, North Carolina, and about 179 miles southwest to Savannah, Georgia. The metro population is listed at 199,630.

sections.h2: How did Florence grow from a rail junction?
sections.html:
Railroads created the city. General William Harllee, president of the Wilmington and Manchester Railroad, built his home at the junction of three lines and named the settlement after his daughter, Florence. The lines were the Wilmington and Manchester, the Northeastern, and the Cheraw and Darlington.

During the Civil War the town was a supply and railroad repair center. The Florence Stockade held between 12,000 and 18,000 Union prisoners of war, and more than 2,800 died there. The burial ground next to it became Florence National Cemetery. The city incorporated on December 24, 1890, two years after the county was created.

Older blocks near the old rail corridors are where you find the pre-war housing stock. Those houses tend to have more deferred maintenance than newer subdivisions, and that is worth thinking about before you list.

sections.h2: What employers shape the Florence housing market?
sections.html:
Health care is the anchor. McLeod Regional Medical Center is the largest employer in the Pee Dee region, and MUSC Florence is the third largest. McLeod runs 453 beds on a 75-acre downtown campus, and MUSC Florence has 420 beds serving eight counties.

Other names tied to the city:

  • GE Healthcare, with an MRI manufacturing facility
  • Honda and a QVC distribution center
  • Patheon, with a pharmaceutical plant and an API research center
  • Duke Energy, with its southeastern headquarters, and AT&T operations
  • Francis Marion University and Florence-Darlington Technical College

After World War II the city was known for textiles, pharmaceuticals and paper, and its economy now mixes commerce, finance, rail and trucking, health care and industry. A hospital shift worker, a university employee and a plant technician each shop for different kinds of homes, so a house that needs repairs may still fit one of those buyers if the price reflects the work.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax inside Florence city limits?
sections.html:
Florence County collects the City of Florence's real estate and personal property taxes. You pay one county bill that includes the city's levy. The City Council sets the millage by June 30 for the July 1 to June 30 fiscal year.

The Florence County Auditor handles vehicle, watercraft, aircraft and business personal property assessments. Bills go to the owner's last known address, and the city says an owner who does not get a bill is still responsible for the tax, so keep the Tax Assessor's Office up to date on where mail goes.

  • Florence County Treasurer: 180 N Irby Street, 843-665-3041
  • Florence County Tax Assessor: 180 N Irby Street, 843-665-3056
  • Florence County Auditor: 180 N Irby Street, 843-665-3088
  • Delinquent Tax Collection: 180 N Irby Street, 843-665-3095
  • City Finance Department: 3rd floor, City Center, 324 W Evans Street, 843-665-3162

County offices are open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. The city's own explanation sits on its property tax payments page.

sections.h2: What are the due dates and penalties for a Florence house?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due by January 15, with penalties of 3 percent on January 16, another 7 percent on February 2 and another 5 percent on March 17. That adds up to 15 percent plus collection costs. State law in Section 12-45-180 sets those steps.

StepAddedCumulative
January 163%3%
February 27%10%
March 175%15%

Real estate bills usually go out around October. A deadline that lands on a weekend or holiday generally moves to the next business day. You can pay in person at the county complex, by mail to 180 N Irby Street, or online through the county's PayStar portal. The city warns against mailing cash. Mailed payments are answered with a receipt by mail.

The state does give a narrow break on title changes. If a house changes hands during the tax year, the notice went to the old owner and the new one got none in time, the treasurer shall waive penalties.

sections.h2: What can a seller do about an assessment?
sections.html:
You can object in writing to the assessor within 90 days after the assessment notice is mailed. State law requires a notice when the assessor raises a value by $1,000 or more, and in a reassessment year the notices are due by October 1. If you got no notice, you may appeal in writing at any time, and the appeal applies to the current year only if it is filed before the first penalty date.

The county page says it reassesses every five years, limits a parcel's increase to 15 percent over that period unless an assessable transfer of interest occurs, and rolls back the millage when overall values rise. The page names tax year 2024 for the most recent cycle and the appeal form is labeled 2027, so ask the Assessor at 843-665-3056 which dates apply to you. Appeals go in writing to the Assessor's office, and the page links a PDF form.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes on a Florence house go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real property and mobile home taxes may lead to a public sale run by Florence County. Before a sale, charges accrue. The county's 2025 list shows $20 for notices in March, $30 for certified mail of a levy in April, $25 for advertising in August and $60 for a land mortgage search in October.

The 2026 sale was set for October 5, 2026, in the parking garage at the County Complex. The owner or a mortgage holder has one year and a day to redeem, and interest rises at 3, 6, 9 and 12 percent of the bid in quarterly steps. Past-due solid waste fees add $25 if paid after March 16. A tax deed is not a warranty deed, and the county says liens can remain.

If you are selling a Florence house with a balance, call 843-665-3095 for the payoff figure before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What does the Florence climate mean for a roof and an air conditioner?
sections.html:
It means long, wet, hot summers. Florence has a humid subtropical climate with mild autumns, winters and springs, and very hot, humid summers. The July mean daily high is about 92.9 degrees Fahrenheit and January's is about 56.9. Annual rainfall averages about 48.12 inches.

Air conditioners, attic ventilation and roofs carry the load, and moisture in crawlspaces is a practical concern. The city is also prone to temperature inversions that can trap ozone and other pollutants. A buyer's inspector will test cooling equipment and look for water stains, so a seller who has not serviced either may want to know that going in.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax for the City of Florence?
faqs.a: Florence County does. The County Treasurer collects City of Florence real estate and personal property taxes on the same county bill.

faqs.q: When is the property tax deadline in Florence, SC?
faqs.a: January 15. A 3 percent penalty starts January 16, and more is added on February 2 and March 17, for 15 percent in total plus costs.
It had 39,899 residents in 2020 and covers 23.49 square miles. It is the county seat of Florence County.

faqs.q: Which hospitals are the largest employers in Florence?
faqs.a: McLeod Regional Medical Center is the largest employer in the Pee Dee region and MUSC Florence is the third largest.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Florence house if I owe taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the balance and any fees must be cleared. Call the Delinquent Tax Office at 843-665-3095 for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.
